content.title: About
content.content: Graham crackers are whole‑grain dry biscuits made from whole wheat, barley and rye. In sandwich form they consist of two crackers with a sweet or creamy filling (such as jam, chocolate spread, or nut butter) placed between them.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Graham crackers were created in the United States in the late 19th century as a healthier alternative to sugary biscuits.
The traditional recipe uses cracked wheat flakes, giving the cracker a characteristic crunch and mild bitterness.
Sandwich versions appeared in the 1930s when manufacturers began adding sweet fillings for children.
Graham crackers are a key ingredient in the American dessert “crackerdough pudding.”
In Russia similar products are sold as “sandwich biscuits with filling.”

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains in the crackers provide fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Graham crackers release energy slowly, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and folate are present, contributing to normal metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many sweet cookies, Graham crackers contain relatively little fat.

items.title: Filling can boost protein
items.content: Using nut butter or cottage‑cheese spread as the filling adds protein to the snack.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: Graham crackers contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar in the filling
items.content: Sweet fillings may be high in sugar, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching their weight.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Consuming large amounts can cause a rapid rise in blood glucose.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Some brands add preservatives or artificial flavors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Graham cracker sandwiches are a convenient snack, suitable for kids’ lunches or as a dessert. They pair well with milk, tea, or can be used as a base for cheesecake‑style desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. For longer shelf life keep refrigerated to prevent the filling from becoming stale.
